scope: Complete per-glyph Korean dictionary order, direction, boundary and form crosscheck. Not exam-body certification.

entries.notes: 氵 three, 士 three, the 冂 and bottom bar of the middle box, and 貝 seven match. The dictionary writes the middle of 賣 as 四 (a short sweep 9 and a small fold 10 inside) while the pinned MM candidate writes 罒 with two inner verticals; neither a sweep nor a fold can be derived from a vertical's own points, so the glyph fails closed. No Ja or Ko candidate with 18 strokes exists in the inventory. Same form difference as 犢·牘·竇 held in the special grade II batches

疒 five and 夂 three (6-8) match, and the first dot (9) descends right in both. The dictionary finishes 冬 with a long stroke rising from the lower left to the right (10) while the pinned MM candidate draws a short dot descending right; the dot's own points cannot give the rising stroke its length or direction, so the glyph fails closed, as 砥 was held for 氐's bar. The inventory lists a 10-stroke Ja candidate that a later batch could pin instead
